data.text:
The Office of the National Water Resources (ONWR) reports that a strong low-pressure system over the lower Andaman Sea and the Strait of Malacca, combined with a moderate northeast monsoon, continues to bring heavy rain to parts of the lower South, especially in Phatthalung, Songkhla, Pattani, Yala, Narathiwat, Trang, and Satun.

Rainfall is expected to ease between November 26–30, though isolated heavy rain may persist as the low-pressure system shifts toward Sumatra and the lower Bay of Bengal. Tropical Storm “Koto”, currently over the Philippines, is forecast to enter the central South China Sea today and intensify before approaching southern Vietnam between November 28–30. The storm will weaken rapidly due to a cold air mass and is not expected to enter Thailand, though it will strengthen the northeast monsoon over upper Thailand.

ONWR warns that seven provinces — Trang, Phatthalung, Songkhla, Satun, Pattani, Yala, and Narathiwat — remain at risk of heavy rainfall exceeding 200 mm through November 27.

Reservoirs nationwide are holding 90% of total capacity, with 83% usable water. Water quality in major rivers remains within standard levels for both consumption and agriculture.

As of 5:00 AM, several rivers and canals in the South remain above bank levels, including Khlong Saothong in Nakhon Si Thammarat, Khlong Duson in Satun, Khlong U-Taphao in Hat Yai, the Pattani River, the Saiburi River in Yala, and Khlong Tanyongmas in Narathiwat. Some levels are falling while others continue to rise.

Flooding has affected 20 provinces and 147 districts as of November 25.

'NO TO DEVELOPMENT AGGRESSION': Cordillera groups hold simultaneous petition submission and protest action in front of the National Commission on Indigenous People office in Quezon City, November 26.

Coinciding with the 71st Annual National Mine Safety and Environment Conference Parade, dubbed as ‘Mine Safety Week’ at Baguio City, the delegation register their urgent demands against the plunder of ancestral lands this week in the metro.

“Over recent years, rapid policy shifts have facilitated the fast-tracking of foreign investment in mining and energy. […] NCIP has advanced amendments to the 2012 FPIC Guidelines without genuine consultation with Indigenous Peoples,” Cordillera Peoples Alliance said in a statement. (via Jhona Reyes Vitor, Gen Feliciano/Altermidya)

data.text:
PHILIPPINES 

🇵🇭 Breaking- All Our Belongings Swept Away’—Tropical Storm Verbena Forces Mass Evacuations in Cebu | 

Nov 25,2025

opical Storm Verbena has unleashed heavy rains, destructive winds, and sudden flooding across the Philippines’ Cebu province, forcing thousands of residents to flee their homes. Entire neighborhoods were inundated within hours, with families reporting that their possessions, documents, and household essentials were “swept away” as waters rose rapidly.

Evacuation centers across Cebu filled overnight as local authorities raced to relocate communities in flood-prone areas. Emergency responders used boats and trucks to rescue stranded families, while landslides and blocked roadways complicated relief operations. Power outages, damaged infrastructure, and overflowing rivers have further strained the province’s response capacity.

Residents say the storm descended with little warning, leaving them scrambling to escape rising waters. Many described losing everything as their homes were swallowed by mud and debris. Local officials have urged continued caution, warning that additional rainfall could worsen conditions.
